diagnosis: I calibrated HBV on daily NSE for 1971-10 to 1997-12, after a one-year warm-up, using DDS. The best run gives NSE 0.814, KGE 0.905, r 0.913 and PBIAS +3.8%, so the model slightly over-predicts total flow. I set the starting stores near their long-term means: soil moisture 250 mm and lower storage 12 mm. Two DDS searches that started from quite different parameter sets ended up in the same place: FC about 375 mm, LP 0.64, BETA 2.3, PERC about 1.5 mm/d, K2 about 0.05, K1 0.26-0.31 and MAXBAS about 3.6 days. NSE barely moved between the two searches (0.813 vs 0.814), so I am fairly confident in the soil and baseflow parameters. The snow parameters, K0 and UZL changed a lot between runs without changing the score, which means the data can't pin them down. That matters little here, because snow is only about 1.5% of precipitation. The remaining errors probably come from the size and timing of individual storm peaks and from slow groundwater storage in the sandstone aquifers. I didn't plot hydrographs, so I can't confirm where in the record the model does worst. I didn't do a split-sample test, so there is no direct check on a separate period. Because both searches agreed, I'd expect NSE around 0.75-0.82 in 1998-2008, but that is an estimate, not a test result.
